svg.text: SIH26097 — PM-AJAY Voice Livelihood Assistant
One core, three doors for the beneficiary, one console for the officer. Every box exists in the repo.
0 — WHO STARTS IT
SC BENEFICIARY — the person the scheme exists for
1 — THREE DOORS INTO THE SAME INTERVIEW
CALLS THE TOLL NUMBER
₹800 keypad phone. No data, no app.
The PS names this channel FIRST.
SENDS A WHATSAPP VOICE NOTE
85.5% of households have a smartphone.
Holds the mic, speaks, releases.
OPENS THE APP
Her own phone, a panchayat kiosk, or an
ASHA / AWW worker at her doorstep.
2 — IDENTITY (phone number is the key — but only one door can show a login)
NO LOGIN — AUTO-IDENTIFY
caller number from start.from
→ hmac(e164, server pepper)
→ phone_hash
A keypad phone cannot log in,
and does not need to.
NO LOGIN — AUTO-IDENTIFY
sender number from the webhook
→ the SAME phone_hash.
So a call on Monday and a voice
note on Tuesday are one person.
LOGIN / SIGN-UP — PHONE OTP
Same number → same phone_hash
→ the earlier IVR conversation
is found and offered.
SKIPPABLE — kiosk mode needs none.
THE RESUME RULE — nobody is ever locked out of a welfare line.
On any re-contact she is offered RESUME or START NEW immediately. No PIN to proceed, ever.
RESUME IS FORWARD-ONLY: ask the next unanswered question; nothing already given is spoken back.
The 4-digit PIN gates only the two actions that REVEAL — the full readback, and the saved recommendation.
3 — THIN ADAPTERS (transport in, prompt out. No interview logic lives here)
IVR ADAPTER
· Exotel AgentStream, bidirectional WebSocket
· 8 kHz L16 mono PCM, base64, 20 ms frames
· VAD endpointing — 12 silent frames = 240 ms
· Adaptive noise floor: a village line is not a lab
· BARGE-IN — she speaks, we send `clear`, kill
the send queue and go back to LISTEN
· DTMF capture: language, yes/no, digits
· Resample 8k → 16k (a format fix, not quality)
· Pre-rendered WAV playback, real-time paced
· Call drops → RESUMABLE, answers persist
WHATSAPP ADAPTER
· Meta Cloud API DIRECT — no reseller markup
· Webhook → media_id → short-lived signed URL
· Download OGG/Opus → decode → 16 kHz PCM
· X-Hub-Signature-256 verified, else dropped
· REPLIES AS A VOICE NOTE, never as text — a
text reply fails people who cannot read
· Prompt audio uploaded once, media id reused
· Reply buttons when expect = enum
· ONE QUESTION PER MESSAGE. Batching saves
₹0.77/head and was rejected: it is a form
APP ADAPTER (Capacitor / Android)
· minSdk 24 — runs on a ₹6,000 handset
· Mic → Web Audio → 16 kHz mono WAV
· Native Android TTS for speech out
· Tap to start, tap to stop, auto-stop on silence
· IndexedDB now / SQLite on device — same row
shape and same CHECKs as Postgres
· OUTBOX syncs itself when signal returns. She
never has to remember to press sync
· On-device fallback ASR when offline
· A full interview completes in aeroplane mode
4 — ONE CONTRACT
POST /v1/turn
{ channel, channelRef, identity, utterance, localeHint } → { say[], expect, state, progress }
No channel knows what is inside. If the FSM ever moves into an adapter, WhatsApp becomes a
second copy of the same seven questions and they disagree by day three.
5 — SPEECH (server-side. This is the part that was unclear: it is NOT on the phone)
SPEECH → TEXT
Audio is sent to the ASR provider, transcribed, and DISCARDED
inside the turn. It is never written to disk, and no
recording_url column exists anywhere in the schema.
THE PROVIDER IS ONE CONFIG VALUE — the switch is the
differentiator, not the model:
Sarvam saaras:v3 LIVE — 228-322 ms measured, Indian region
Bhashini / ULCA the sovereign path, free non-commercial
IndicConformer MIT, self-hosted — flip it on stage
Vosk on-device ~50 MB, genuinely offline, for the kiosk
THE DIALECT PROBLEM, STATED HONESTLY
Maithili IS covered (mai-IN) — it is Eighth Schedule.
Bhojpuri 5.05 cr · Rajasthani 2.58 cr
Chhattisgarhi 1.62 cr · Magahi 1.27 cr
≈ 11 crore speakers with NO model at Sarvam, at Bhashini,
or anywhere open-source. They go to the Hindi model because
there is nothing else to send them to.
We do NOT claim a dialect model. The error is absorbed by the
lexicon below, and WER is published beside field accuracy.
Dual-pass for those four: a second call with language_code=unknown.
6 — EXTRACTION LADDER (this replaces “is the reply complex?” — the decision is per FIELD, cheapest first)
RUNG 0 DTMF keypress / on-screen tap ₹0 · 0 ms · 0 WER
RUNG 1 VERNACULAR LEXICON — phonetic + fuzzy over ASR n-best ~₹0 · ~5 ms · ~70% of turns
RUNG 2 Numeric / class-level regex — “8th”, “दसवीं”, “बारह साल” ~₹0 · ~2 ms · Q1 and Q2-years
RUNG 3 LLM — ONLY “which of these N options did they mean?” 1 call · 400-1200 ms · uncommon
RUNG 4 Spoken confirmation — catches whatever the rest got wrong 1 turn · ~4 s
STOP ON THE FIRST RUNG THAT FIRES.
Low confidence is a RE-ASK, not an error — which is what a
considerate human interviewer does anyway.
conf ≥ 0.85 → confirm
0.55 – 0.85 → explicit spoken readback
< 0.55 → re-ask, max 2
after 2 → DTMF fallback, else DEFER and move on
WHAT THE LLM ACTUALLY RECEIVES
The transcript, and a list of options. That is all.
No name · no phone number · no district · no caste marker.
OpenRouter for the common case — cheap and swappable.
Sarvam-M as the one-config-value sovereign switch, because
“we can run this on Indian infrastructure” is a sentence
worth being able to say in a MoSJE room.
7 — THE CORE (this was the empty box. It is the entire product)
1. IDENTITY & SESSION RESOLVE — phone_hash → beneficiary. Answer rows hang off beneficiary_id, NEVER session_id.
That one line is what lets a dropped call on Monday finish on a kiosk on Tuesday.
2. INTERVIEW FSM — seven PS fields, in order, not an agent
LANG_SELECT
→ Q0 village / block (registration metadata, not an 8th field)
→ CONSENT ≤15 s, spoken, logged with its script_version
→ Q1 education
→ Q2 family trade + years ← the eligibility inputs
→ Q3 current livelihood
→ Q4 skills & interests
→ Q5 mobility / constraints
→ Q6 self-employment vs wage
→ Q7 local economy
→ READBACK all seven, spoken yes
→ RECOMMEND → NEXT_STEP → CLOSE
Q5 may branch to GUARDIAN_CHECK — on DECISIONAL CAPACITY,
not on disability. DPDP Rule 11, not Rule 10.
4. RECOMMENDER — gate, THEN rank. Never rank then gate
STAGE 0 ELIGIBILITY GATE — rules only. No model, no score.
NSQF entry rules vs (education ∪ experience substitution)
Returns THREE buckets, always:
ELIGIBLE · NEAR_MISS (with the exact gap) · INELIGIBLE
STAGE 0.5 PM-DAKSH ROUTING — the guidelines forbid overlap
by name, so where PM-DAKSH fits, we hand off
STAGE 1 RETRIEVE over the eligible set only
STAGE 2 RANK — weights written down and versioned,
plus a SPREAD PENALTY so concentration is priced in
STAGE 3 EXPLAIN ×3 — beneficiary / officer / auditor,
all from the same scored object
3. PROFILE — per field: value, confidence, method (DTMF | LEXICON | REGEX | LLM), asr_engine, confirmed_at.
raw_transcript is ERASED AT CONFIRM — a Postgres CHECK makes keeping it impossible. The audio was already gone.
“We keep neither the voice nor the words, only the confirmed answer.”
8 — TWO OUTPUTS, NOT ONE
B1 — TO THE BENEFICIARY, SPOKEN, ≤ 60 s
Back down the SAME channel she arrived on.
· Top 3 qualifications she is actually ELIGIBLE for
· 1 NEAR-MISS with the exact gap — “one more year”, or
“do the Level 2 course first”. THIS IS R4's FOURTH OUTPUT
· One plain sentence of reason each. No scheme jargon
· PM-DAKSH hand-off + ₹1,500/month stipend where it applies
· ₹50,000 asset grant (needs a bank loan) where it applies
· What to do on Monday, and the nearest centre
· Repeatable on demand — call back and press 9
B2 — TO POSTGRES, AND THEN TO THE OFFICER
Every recommendation is stored with:
weights_version · engine_version · nqr_snapshot_sha · the inputs
In 2030 somebody will ask why this person was sent to this trade.
The answer has to be a ROW, not a prompt.
NOTE THE DIRECTION: adapters NEVER write to the database.
Everything passes through the core first — otherwise the gate
and the FSM can be bypassed, and the register quietly fills
with ungated rows nobody can defend.
9 — TRUE EVERYWHERE, ON EVERY CHANNEL
PRIVACY, BY CONSTRUCTION
· Audio discarded inside the turn. No
recording_url column exists.
· raw_transcript erased at CONFIRM — enforced
by a DB CHECK, on the server AND in the
on-device SQLite schema.
· Raw phone number never stored — only
hmac(e164, pepper), and the pepper never
leaves the server.
· Consent is an FSM STATE, logged with its
script version, withdrawable, and it names
all four surfaces.
· Guardian branch fires on decisional
capacity, never on disability.
CROSS-CHANNEL RESUME
One person, one profile. Sessions are
disposable.
IVR Monday 11:02, drops at Q4
→ WhatsApp Monday 18:40, resumes AT Q4
→ kiosk Tuesday, finishes Q5-Q7
Confirmed answers are immutable. Only
unconfirmed fields are ever re-asked.
Several people per handset is the NORMAL
case here, carried by (phone_hash, ordinal)
— 51.6% of rural women own no phone.
PROVENANCE
· NQR official export — 2,814 rows, sha-
stamped. Fields the source omits are NULL,
never guessed.
· NO INVENTED QP CODES, EVER. Prototype rows
carry qp_code = NULL and the UI says so
in amber on every recommendation.
· NSQF 2023 entry table — typed by hand,
under 100 rows. This IS the gate.
· NCO-2015 is a SIGNAL ONLY — NCVET found
156 of 2,157 mis-mapped, 256 unmappable.
· Opportunity rows carry source + source_date
or are excluded from the Plan export.
WHY AN FSM AND NOT AN LLM AGENT: every turn is replayable, every extraction is a logged (transcript → value, confidence)
pair, and the model can never invent an eighth question in front of a jury. When CAG audits this in 2029, the answer is a row.
THE OFFICER — a different person, a different path
DISTRICT OFFICER / PIU
OPENS THE CONSOLE
Desktop or tablet, indoors, literate.
Never touches an adapter or the FSM.
ROLE-BASED LOGIN
officer · mobiliser · admin
Postgres RLS scopes every query to that
person's own district. Nobody sees the
country, and a mobiliser sees only her
own villages.
OFFICER CONSOLE
Reads the database directly.
It is not an interview, it is a report —
so it does NOT go through /v1/turn.
Fed by B2, on the left.
Four of the five “Basic Issues under GIA” live below.
BASIC ISSUE 1 — PERSPECTIVE PLAN
Aggregated confirmed demand becomes the
statutory artefact.
· 3.5-4× the notional allocation
· multi-year horizon
· DL-PACC submits via the portal
*** DUE THE FIRST WEEK OF APRIL ***
Demand data arriving in July is worthless.
The differentiator is the FORMAT and the
DATE, not the dashboard.
BASIC ISSUE 2 — IDENTIFICATION
AND FINANCIAL LINKAGE
· Verified beneficiary register
· Consent register — every row carries the
script_version she actually heard
· Financial-literacy module flag, compulsory
in every course (Ch.3 ¶7A.a.iv)
· ₹50,000 asset-grant eligibility flag,
conditional on a bank loan
BASIC ISSUE 3 — PLACEMENT
outcome: RECOMMENDED → ENROLLED →
CERTIFIED → PLACED → DROPPED
Updated from the mobiliser's call list,
NOT from a new officer screen.
Guidelines mandate 70% placement.
CAG measured PMKVY at 41%.
Turns “demand” into “demand AND delivery”,
which is what a DL-PACC argues about.
BASIC ISSUE 4 — COORDINATION
Batch export, convergence-shaped:
“240 people in this block want and are
eligible for QP AGR/Q1201”
→ SSDM · DSC · NSFDC / NSKFDC
→ training partners
Plus PM-DAKSH routing counts.
Per-district, per-project, per-beneficiary.
BASIC ISSUE 5 — NO GROUND STAFF
“Inadequate technical and support team at
ground level” — the scheme's own written
statement of why automation.
The assistant IS the ground-level team.
Every screen we add is a screen somebody
must be trained on out of a 5% admin
budget — so the mobiliser gets ONE list,
not a console.
AND THE ONE THAT DECIDES IT
MEASURE SPREAD, NOT JUST RELEVANCE.
CAG: 40% of all certifications in 10 job-roles.
90.35% of “Green Jobs” in Safai Karmchari alone.
If our recommendations concentrate the same
way, we have automated the failure with
better UX. So the ranker carries a spread
penalty and the console plots the
distribution against that line.
district
aggregation
feeds the
console
